children.description: Backend-owned decisions. Current migration covers CPU remediation and its existing scheduling/history consumers, not every backend setting.
Backend subscriptions publish current values; readers do not sample.

simple.description: Shared subscription-source stop buffer after a single request ends, one cell per memory/CPU tier (tier 1 first; tier 3 is the former single value). Zero disables the buffer; keeping a source in use never schedules sampling.

How long the Windows service identity resolver reuses one service-to-process snapshot, one cell per memory/CPU tier (tier 1 first; tier 3 is the former single value). Zero re-reads the service list on every resolution.
Frame-time window the performance overlay channel summarizes in each delivery.

complex.description: Backend-lifetime named observation demand; enabled controls continuous low-rate sampling, bounded rings and sustained-growth thresholds. Report readers never control observation. reported_item_capacity defaults to 4096, accepts 1-16384 active and history items, and never evicts; users can clear history to free capacity.

Backend notification owner. retained_count defaults to 64 and accepts 1-1024 notifications; a new notification beyond it evicts the oldest. Notifications only deliver; the event itself stays in its report or page.
Host memory protection action records. record_capacity defaults to 4096 and accepts 1-16384 records; a full report never evicts, counts what it could not record, and clearing history frees capacity.

Targeted recording. default_maximum_duration_seconds applies when a request names no duration; maximum_duration_limit_seconds is the largest accepted duration; sample_interval_ms is the cadence of the target process check while recording (items carry their own intervals); maximum_report_kib caps the stored bytes of one report (a start whose estimate exceeds it is rejected, a running report stops storing and records a size-limit gap); exit_confirmation_ticks is how many consecutive checks must find every known target process gone before the recording ends with all-processes-exited; no_process_ticks is how many consecutive ready checks without any target process end it with no-process.

Bounded native kernel ETW working state and immutable publications, plus the real-time kernel session's ETW buffer pool (session_buffer_kib per buffer, session_minimum_buffers at start; TraceEvent sets the maximum to 5/4 of the minimum plus 10, and ETW raises the minimum to 2 per logical processor). Capacity exhaustion is a reported failure.

children.description: Per-process CPU core observations, distinct from a weighted CPU score.

simple.description: CPU residency observation window, not algorithm history retention.

complex.description: Actual per-logical-processor execution durations, not context-switch counts.

children.description: Scheduling reads shared snapshots and requests persistent backend subscriptions.

simple.description: Scheduler background subscription interval. The current explicit choice is 0.2 Hz. Rebuilding and restarting changes the startup subscriptions.

children.description: Transition decisions, game startup grace and failure retry are independent quantities.

simple.description: Existing confirmation votes. This is not a CPU history length or a score average.
Existing game-start grace. It does not implement lower boost exit thresholds.
Retry delay following a failed action, not a cooldown following success.

complex.description: Explicit entry and lower exit thresholds for game enhancement.
complex.pending_reason: Separate entry/exit quantities and calibration follow the corrected unique CPU score; consecutive votes alone do not implement this policy.

complex.description: Game system notifications: confirmed enhancement and an independently switchable reminder when a running game has not entered enhancement within its configured observation time.
complex.pending_reason: NativeUi delivery, persisted switches and named observation duration are not wired to existing game/effect facts yet. Reminders do not retune B, force enhancement or add frontend warnings.

children.description: Placement is not the CPU score denominator.

simple.description: First-use actual GPU API observation window inside the original placement action deadline; no separate discovery cycle or retry.
Persistent per-image empty Present observation expires after 86400 seconds by default; retry requires a subsequent inventory or GPU-use fact. PID replacement and observer restart do not reset it.

complex.description: Serial GPU preparation and controlled window execution: explicit window count, shared cleanup allowance, separate preparation/window payload bounds and pipe buffers. All work shares the original action deadline; no retries or synchronous fallback.

simple.description: Existing placement action total deadline, shared by policy and serial GPU window work, including cleanup. Not a fresh timeout per window.

complex.description: Native placement-session game core/CCD occupancy hysteresis and software reservations. Other software avoids the reservation; the owner is not locked. CPU effects use the existing reversible placement transaction.

children.description: One software-scoring definition; CPU and GPU remain separate resource dimensions.

complex.description: The sole native scorer uses its own base_score (0 to maximum base importance, default 100). CPU and memory each add base_score times their direct free-capacity ratio once per software, without recipient counts, state modifiers or CPU capacity compensation. GPU share retains base_score times the product of four free ratios divided by eligible process count.
Existing shared base-importance tier boundaries, not software-kind default scores.

children.description: Physical-core usage is weighted by the compiled per-core capacity and divided by the shared machine baseline. CPU-input and score smoothing remain separate pending consumers.

complex.description: Compile each physical core's logical sibling count, fixed reciprocal and logical-to-physical mapping from startup topology. Runtime multiplies execution duration by the compiled share; it does not discover topology or count active threads. Separate from CPU-Z weights and B.

simple.description: One machine reference B for all software, independent of core performance weights.
Retained CPU input rounds requested by the CPU algorithm; retention does not prescribe an average.
simple.pending_reason: The user requested three CPU rounds. The CPU history consumer is not yet connected; the stateless welfare-capacity intermediate is not a data item or history consumer.

simple.description: Independent retained score rounds; five rounds is an example, not an adopted product default.
simple.pending_reason: Score history and its independent algorithm have not been implemented or calibrated.

complex.description: Current CPU runtime-state multiplier table, consumed in ABI state order.

Compiled per-physical-core reference weights. Complete manual vectors or known homogeneous relative units are available; unadmitted CPU-Z research and heuristic topology display scores are not automatic weights.
Algorithm consuming the requested CPU history, independent of the cache contract.
complex.pending_reason: The current scorer uses instantaneous weighted physical-core CPU. CPU input smoothing has not been connected.

complex.description: Independent score smoothing after the unique weighted CPU formula.
complex.pending_reason: No score-history consumer exists. Do not treat three transition votes as score smoothing.

simple.description: Reset the service crash counter after this many seconds without a crash.

children.description: Backend access-request lifetime, used by the bounded local approval flow.

simple.description: Lifetime in milliseconds for an unbound local access request and its one-time key delivery.

children.description: Fixed-capacity backend control for business-block workers, queues, readers, arenas, and failure reasons.

simple.description: Number of workers in the native backend business-block scheduler.
Maximum completed business-block results retained for diagnostics.
Maximum completed business-block results awaiting consumption.
Maximum business-block state readers admitted by native control.
Maximum byte size of a retained business-block reader payload.
Byte capacity of each native business-block worker arena.
Maximum characters retained for a business-block failure reason.

children.description: Optional hardware helpers and control writers: availability, request and stop timing, fan curve feed, EC channel. Availability checks never start a helper.

simple.description: Check changeable prerequisites only while unavailable. Zero disables polling; installation events still update availability.

Longest wait for one hardware helper request: hardware bridge requests and command-queue entries, and Fan Control Core inventory discovery. A timed-out request keeps its resource until the helper completes.

complex.description: Hardware bridge helper process timing. diagnostic_drain_timeout_ms bounds the wait for diagnostic output when the helper exits (zero does not wait); stop_timeout_ms bounds each stop step (gate, end of input, kill); reading_interval_ms is the helper's readings section interval.

Fan curve temperature feed. interval_ms is both the temperature subscription interval and the push interval to Fan Control Core; it must stay short because the firmware hands the fans back after a few seconds without input. maximum_sample_age_ms is the oldest temperature sample still forwarded; older samples are dropped, never replayed.

Uniwill ACPI-WMI EC channel. lock_wait_ms bounds the wait for the cross-process EC channel lock; a timeout skips the transaction. A register read counts only after agreeing_reads identical values within read_attempts reads; otherwise it reports no value.

simple.description: Maximum retained report observations after a native required-count query. Default 16384; accepts the initial profile limit through 536870912. Native persistence capacity and resident-byte budget also apply. One reserve and retry per observation; no eviction.

children.description: 内存与 CPU 取舍: five cells per option, tier 1 (least memory, most CPU) to tier 5 (least CPU, most memory). Each cell is {value, category}; aggressive cells appear only in tiers 1 and 5. The stop buffer and service identity cache options are the five-value points monitoring/build/simple/0 and /1. The settings owner resolves the user's tier and per-option values; option owners read the effective value on their next use.

complex.description: System.GC.Gen0MaxBudget in bytes, written into the installed service and NativeUi runtimeconfig files; takes effect after the process restarts. Null removes the key (not set: the runtime sizes gen0 from the L3 cache).
System.GC.ConserveMemory (0-9), written into the installed service and NativeUi runtimeconfig files; takes effect after the process restarts.

Lowest memory mode the program's own Ledger tables may use: optimize returns unused Ledger memory at every check; autoThrifty, auto and autoGenerous choose from free memory with saving, current and retaining thresholds; unrestricted never returns it proactively. Declared and resolved; the Ledger owner reads it from step 2 of the memory/CPU tier design.

When the process-inventory kernel-table workspace is returned: releaseAfterUse frees it after every parse; shrinkAfterNLowReads shrinks it after N consecutive reads that use at most a quarter; keepPeak never shrinks and reserves the previous peak after a release. Read at the next borrow.

How native work areas grow: exactRows sizes them to the actual rows and shrinks them after use; rows125, rows150 and rows200 grow to that percentage of the actual rows and shrink on low use; reserveCapacity reserves the capacity limit at once. Declared and resolved; the native owners read it from step 2 of the memory/CPU tier design.
How long the browser runtime catalog reuses one snapshot. Zero re-reads on every request. Read at the next request.
How long the platform sensor reader reuses one sensor snapshot. Zero re-reads on every request. Read at the next request.
How long the storage owner reuses one storage capability snapshot. Zero re-reads on every request. Read at the next request.
Entries the GPU renderer absence cache holds before it clears the whole table. Read at the next insertion.
Most native file-query sessions open at once; sessions are built on demand up to this limit and the published query_session_count and resident budget. Read at the next acquisition.
File-query sessions built when the pool is created, at most file_query_sessions_max. Read when the next pool is created.
What happens to a returned file-query session that no waiter takes: close closes it, keep keeps it for the next query. Read at the next return.
